strengths: Good athletic setup and stance width
Decent shoulder turn in the backswing
improvements: Over-the-top downswing path
Early extension through impact losing spine angle
Casting and early release of the hands
analysis.key_fault: Over-the-top downswing transition combined with early extension at impact, leading to an out-to-in club path.

drill_1.name: The Pump Drill
drill_1.description: Take the club to the top of your backswing. Start your downswing by bringing your hands down to hip level while keeping your back to the target, then pump back to the top. Do this twice before letting the third swing release through impact. This helps feel an inside-out path.

drill_2.name: Butt-to-Wall Drill
drill_2.description: Stand a few inches away from a wall without a club. Take your posture and make a simulated swing. Ensure your trail glute touches the wall on the backswing, and your lead glute touches it on the downswing and impact. This prevents early extension.

drill_3.name: Alignment Stick Path Drill
drill_3.description: Place an alignment stick in the ground 3 feet behind your ball at a 45-degree angle, matching your shaft plane. Practice swinging under the stick on the downswing to force an inside-out path.

analysis.summary: Your swing has a solid foundation with a strong setup and balanced finish. To improve consistency and power, focus on starting the downswing with your lower body to prevent an over-the-top path, and maintain your spine angle through impact to avoid early extension.

setup.observation: Stance is wide and stable, suitable for a driver. Ball position is forward. Spine angle is decent but hands hang slightly low.

backswing.observation: Good shoulder rotation, but the club gets slightly flat on the takeaway and then lifts at the top, crossing the line.

downswing.observation: The downswing is initiated by the upper body, causing the club to come over the top with an out-to-in path.

impact.observation: Early extension is present as the hips move toward the ball, causing the spine to straighten prematurely.

follow_through.observation: Good extension and balanced finish, though weight transfer is slightly limited by the early extension.

metrics.impact_position: hips cleared slightly late, hands slightly behind ideal lead-side lag

strengths: Eyes positioned well over the ball
improvements: Head peeking and moving too early
Wristy stroke instead of shoulder pendulum
Inconsistent acceleration through impact
analysis.key_fault: Early head movement (peeking) and wrist-dominated stroke leading to inconsistent distance control and face angle at impact.

drill_1.name: Listen for the Cup Drill
drill_1.description: Practice short putts (3-5 feet) with your eyes focused on the ball's original position. Do not look up until you hear the ball drop into the cup. Perform 20 reps.

drill_2.name: Coin Under Ball Drill
drill_2.description: Place a small coin directly under the golf ball. Make your putting stroke and keep your eyes focused on the coin after the ball is struck. Do 15 reps.

drill_3.name: Metronome Tempo Practice
drill_3.description: Use a metronome app set to 70-75 BPM. Sync your backswing to the first beat and impact/follow-through to the second beat to establish a smooth, pendulum tempo. Practice for 10 minutes.

analysis.summary: Your putting setup is solid with good posture and eye alignment. However, the stroke is hindered by early head movement (peeking) and a wristy motion rather than a smooth shoulder-led pendulum, which affects distance control and face angle consistency.

setup.observation: Good posture with a comfortable spine angle. Eyes appear to be well-positioned over the ball. Grip looks relaxed.

backswing.observation: Short backswing, but initiated slightly with the wrists rather than a pure shoulder rock.

downswing.observation: Slightly jabby transition. The head begins to rotate toward the target before impact is fully completed.

impact.observation: Inconsistent face contact due to early head movement. Hands are active, causing minor wrist breakdown.

follow_through.observation: Abbreviated follow-through. The head looks up immediately, preventing a stable, low release of the putter head.

metrics.impact_position: Hands slightly behind or even with the ball

strengths: Good posture and spine angle at setup
Controlled backswing length for a wedge shot
improvements: Slightly arm-dominated swing with limited torso rotation
Steep downswing angle
Lack of forward shaft lean at impact
analysis.key_fault: Arm-dominated motion with limited body rotation, leading to a slightly steep angle of attack.

drill_1.name: Body Rotation Pitching
drill_1.description: Place a glove under your lead armpit. Practice hitting 30-yard pitch shots keeping the glove trapped to force your torso to rotate with your arms.

drill_2.name: Alignment Stick Lead Wrist Drill
drill_2.description: Hold an alignment stick against the shaft of your wedge extending up past your lead hip. Practice chipping without letting the stick hit your lead side to maintain shaft lean.

drill_3.name: Feet Together Drill
drill_3.description: Hit half-wedge shots with your feet completely together to improve balance, tempo, and upper-body rotation.

analysis.summary: Your setup is solid with good posture. The swing is a controlled partial wedge shot, but it is quite arm-dominated with limited hip and shoulder rotation, leading to a slightly steep downswing.

setup.observation: Good posture with a straight spine and appropriate knee flex. Stance width is narrow and suitable for a wedge shot.

backswing.observation: Abbreviated backswing for a pitch shot. The movement is mostly controlled by the arms with minimal hip or shoulder turn.

downswing.observation: Downswing is initiated primarily by the hands and arms, creating a slightly steep path into the ball.

impact.observation: Decent contact, but the hands are relatively neutral rather than pressed forward, reducing optimal compression.

follow_through.observation: Abbreviated finish matching the backswing length. Good balance, though the body rotation is limited.

improvements: Over-the-top downswing path

analysis.key_fault: Over-the-top downswing path combined with early extension at impact, leading to inconsistent contact and a steep angle of attack.

drill_1.name: Pump Drill
drill_1.description: Take the club to the top, start the downswing by pulling the arms down to hip level while keeping the back to the target, then return to the top. Do this twice before making a full swing to feel the proper downswing sequence.

drill_2.name: Chair/Wall Drill for Early Extension
drill_2.description: Setup with your glutes touching a wall or chair. During the backswing and downswing, maintain contact with the wall to prevent early extension.

drill_3.name: Alignment Stick Gate Drill
drill_3.description: Place an alignment stick in the ground at a 45-degree angle just behind and outside your target line to force an inside-out swing path.

analysis.summary: Your swing has a solid foundation but suffers from a steep, over-the-top downswing and early extension at impact. Improving your posture at setup and focusing on a lower-body-initiated transition will greatly improve contact consistency.

setup.observation: Posture is slightly slouched in the upper spine. Stance width is solid and club is aligned well with the target.

backswing.observation: Takeaway is slightly inside, leading to a lift at the top. Shoulder turn is somewhat restricted, limiting depth.

downswing.observation: Transition starts with the upper body, casting the club outward and creating a steep, over-the-top path.

impact.observation: Early extension is present as the hips move toward the ball, causing the spine to straighten and leading to a slight scoop/flip at impact.

follow_through.observation: Finish is somewhat upright and abbreviated due to the early extension, with incomplete rotation through the target.

metrics.impact_position: hands level with or slightly behind the ball

strengths: Solid posture and alignment at setup
Stable lower body throughout the stroke
Good eye position relative to the ball
improvements: Minimize wrist breakdown during the stroke
Rock the shoulders instead of using the hands
Keep the putter head lower to the ground on the backstroke
analysis.key_fault: Excessive wrist action (handsy stroke) leading to inconsistent face angle and distance control.

drill_1.name: Ruler / Splint Drill
drill_1.description: Place a ruler or alignment stick under your lead watch strap or glove, extending down the back of your hand. Practice making strokes without the ruler digging into your forearm, which prevents wrist breakdown.

drill_2.name: Shoulder Rocking Drill
drill_2.description: Cross your arms over your chest, placing your hands on opposite shoulders. Practice rocking your shoulders back and forth without moving your hips or hands to feel a true pendulum motion.

drill_3.name: Two-Tee Gate Drill
drill_3.description: Place two tees just wider than your putter head on the putting green. Practice making strokes through the gate to ensure a centered, consistent strike.

analysis.summary: Your putting setup is solid with good posture, but the stroke is highly dependent on wrist movement rather than a shoulder-controlled pendulum. Quieting the hands will greatly improve your distance control and directional consistency.

setup.observation: Good posture and alignment. Hands are positioned slightly low, which might encourage wrist play. Ball position is neutral.

backswing.observation: The backstroke is initiated primarily by the hands and wrists rather than a shoulder turn, causing the putter head to lift too quickly.

downswing.observation: Forward stroke relies on hand acceleration, making it difficult to control speed consistently.

impact.observation: Impact is made near the center, but the wrist angle is breaking down, which can lead to loft and direction inconsistencies.

follow_through.observation: The follow-through shows a noticeable flip of the wrists, with the putter head rising too high too quickly.

metrics.impact_position: hands slightly behind the putter head due to wrist breakdown

drill_1.name: Keep the Lead Arm Straight Drill
drill_1.description: Practice half-swings focusing on keeping the lead arm extended and straight to the top of the backswing. Do 20 slow-motion reps daily.

drill_2.name: Step-Through Drill
drill_2.description: To fix hanging back, take a step forward with your trail foot immediately after impact to force proper weight transfer to the lead side. Do 15 reps.

drill_3.name: Pump Drill
drill_3.description: From the top of the backswing, pump the hands down to hip level twice while maintaining wrist hinge before releasing on the third swing. 10 minutes of practice.

analysis.summary: Your swing has a decent foundation at setup, but suffers from a collapsed lead arm at the top and casting on the downswing, which prevents proper weight transfer and consistent compression.

setup.observation: Stance width is good for a driver. Ball position is forward as required. Spine angle is slightly upright but acceptable.

backswing.observation: Lead arm collapses significantly at the top of the swing, causing an overswing and loss of structure. Wrist hinge is early.

downswing.observation: Downswing starts with an early release (casting) of the wrists. Weight remains on the trail foot instead of shifting forward.

impact.observation: Flipping/scooping motion at impact with hands behind the ball. Weight is hung back on the trail side.

follow_through.observation: Finish is slightly unbalanced due to the weight staying back. Lead arm exhibits a slight chicken-wing pattern.

  <rect width="400" height="500" fill="#1a2e1a"/>

  <!-- Arrowhead marker definition -->
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrowRed" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="10" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
      <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="#e87a5a"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="200" y="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" font-family="monospace">TOP OF BACKSWING</text>
  <!-- Subtitle -->
  <text x="200" y="46" text-anchor="middle" fill="#f5f0e8" font-size="11" font-family="monospace">Collapsed arm, casting, weight hanging back</text>

  <!-- Ground line -->
  <line x1="60" y1="430" x2="340" y2="430" stroke="#4a6a4a" stroke-width="2"/>

  <!-- ===== STICK FIGURE ===== -->
  <!-- Golfer at top of backswing, weight on trail foot (right), collapsed lead arm -->

  <!-- FEET / ANKLES -->
  <!-- Trail foot (right) - bearing weight, GREEN ish neutral -->
  <circle cx="230" cy="425" r="5" fill="#f5f0e8" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="1"/>
  <!-- Lead foot (left) -->
  <circle cx="165" cy="425" r="5" fill="#f5f0e8" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- LEGS -->
  <!-- Trail leg (right) - weight hanging back, slightly bent, RED fault -->
  <!-- Trail ankle to knee -->
  <line x1="230" y1="425" x2="225" y2="365" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Trail knee to hip -->
  <line x1="225" y1="365" x2="220" y2="305" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Trail knee joint -->
  <circle cx="225" cy="365" r="5" fill="#e87a5a" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Lead leg (left) - straighter, some weight -->
  <line x1="165" y1="425" x2="175" y2="365" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>
  <line x1="175" y1="365" x2="195" y2="305" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Lead knee joint -->
  <circle cx="175" cy="365" r="5" fill="#f5f0e8" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- HIPS - centered but shifted trail side -->
  <!-- Hip line -->
  <line x1="195" y1="305" x2="220" y2="305" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Hip joints -->
  <circle cx="195" cy="305" r="5" fill="#e87a5a" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="1"/>
  <circle cx="220" cy="305" r="5" fill="#e87a5a" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- SPINE / TORSO - tilted slightly, rotated into backswing -->
  <!-- Hip center to shoulder center -->
  <line x1="207" y1="305" x2="200" y2="230" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>

  <!-- SHOULDERS - rotated, right shoulder high, left lower -->
  <!-- Shoulder line -->
  <line x1="175" y1="238" x2="228" y2="222" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Left shoulder (lead) -->
  <circle cx="175" cy="238" r="6" fill="#f5f0e8" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="1"/>
  <!-- Right shoulder (trail) -->
  <circle cx="228" cy="222" r="6" fill="#f5f0e8" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- HEAD -->
  <circle cx="205" cy="195" r="18" fill="none" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Neck -->
  <line x1="205" y1="213" x2="203" y2="228" stroke="#f5f0e8" stroke-width="3"/>

  <!-- ===== ARMS ===== -->

  <!-- TRAIL ARM (right) - straight/braced - GREEN (correct) -->
  <!-- Trail shoulder to trail elbow -->
  <line x1="228" y1="222" x2="258" y2="190" stroke="#6abf6a" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Trail elbow -->
  <circle cx="258" cy="190" r="5" fill="#6abf6a" stroke="#6abf6a" stroke-width="1"/>
  <!-- Trail elbow to trail hand -->
  <line x1="258" y1="190" x2="272" y2="162" stroke="#6abf6a" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Trail hand -->
  <circle cx="272" cy="162" r="5" fill="#6abf6a" stroke="#6abf6a" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- LEAD ARM (left) - COLLAPSED / BENT - RED fault -->
  <!-- Lead shoulder to lead elbow - bent inward, collapsed -->
  <line x1="175" y1="238" x2="218" y2="200" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="4"/>
  <!-- Lead elbow - significantly bent, showing collapse -->
  <circle cx="218" cy="200" r="6" fill="#e87a5a" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="1"/>
  <!-- Lead elbow to lead hand - bent back sharply -->
  <line x1="218" y1="200" x2="265" y2="168" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="4"/>
  <!-- Lead hand meeting trail hand -->
  <circle cx="265" cy="168" r="6" fill="#e87a5a" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- CLUB - steep plane, laid off due to collapse -->
  <!-- Grip area to clubhead -->
  <line x1="268" y1="165" x2="220" y2="118" stroke="#c8a84b" stroke-width="2"/>
  <!-- Clubhead -->
  <rect x="212" y="110" width="12" height="8" fill="#c8a84b" stroke="#c8a84b" stroke-width="1" transform="rotate(-20, 218, 114)"/>

  <!-- ===== FAULT INDICATORS / ARROWS ===== -->

  <!-- Arrow 1: Collapsed lead arm -->
  <path d="M 145,195 C 155,195 165,198 178,202" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrowRed)"/>
  <text x="70" y="185" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="13" font-family="monospace">Arm Collapse!</text>

  <!-- Arrow 2: Lead elbow bent (overcollapsed) -->
  <path d="M 200,230 C 208,220 212,212 216,204" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrowRed)"/>
  <text x="155" y="248" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="13" font-family="monospace">Early Bend</text>

  <!-- Arrow 3: Weight on trail foot -->
  <path d="M 275,400 C 265,410 252,418 238,422" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrowRed)"/>
  <text x="275" y="398" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="13" font-family="monospace">Weight Back!</text>

  <!-- Arrow 4: Steep/laid off club / early wrist set -->
  <path d="M 195,118 C 205,120 215,118 222,116" stroke="#e87a5a" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrowRed)"/>
  <text x="130" y="112" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="13" font-family="monospace">Laid-Off Club</text>

  <!-- ===== SWING PLANE GUIDE LINE (reference) ===== -->
  <line x1="175" y1="425" x2="270" y2="145" stroke="#4a6a4a" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="6,4" opacity="0.6"/>
  <text x="282" y="140" fill="#4a6a4a" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">Plane</text>

  <!-- ===== METRICS PANEL ===== -->
  <rect x="10" y="452" width="380" height="40" fill="#0d1f0d" rx="4" opacity="0.8"/>
  <text x="20" y="467" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">Path: Out-to-In</text>
  <text x="108" y="467" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">| Tempo: 3.2:1</text>
  <text x="210" y="467" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">| Plane: Steep</text>
  <text x="298" y="467" fill="#c8a84b" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">| Hips: 35°</text>
  <text x="20" y="483" fill="#f5f0e8" font-size="10" font-family="monospace">Weight: Trail Side  | Impact: Hands Behind | Casting: YES</text>

</svg>

improvements: Lead arm collapses at the top of the backswing
Casting and early release on the downswing
Hanging back on the trail foot through impact
analysis.key_fault: Severe collapse of the lead arm at the top of the backswing combined with casting on the downswing, leading to a loss of power and inconsistent contact.

drill_1.name: Keep the Lead Arm Straight Drill
drill_1.description: Practice half-swings focusing on keeping the lead arm extended and straight to the top of the backswing. Do 20 slow-motion reps daily.

drill_2.name: Step-Through Drill
drill_2.description: To fix hanging back, take a step forward with your trail foot immediately after impact to force proper weight transfer to the lead side. Do 15 reps.

drill_3.name: Pump Drill
drill_3.description: From the top of the backswing, pump the hands down to hip level twice while maintaining wrist hinge before releasing on the third swing. 10 minutes of practice.

analysis.summary: Your swing has a decent foundation at setup, but suffers from a collapsed lead arm at the top and casting on the downswing, which prevents proper weight transfer and consistent compression.

setup.observation: Stance width is good for a driver. Ball position is forward as required. Spine angle is slightly upright but acceptable.

backswing.observation: Lead arm collapses significantly at the top of the swing, causing an overswing and loss of structure. Wrist hinge is early.

downswing.observation: Downswing starts with an early release (casting) of the wrists. Weight remains on the trail foot instead of shifting forward.

impact.observation: Flipping/scooping motion at impact with hands behind the ball. Weight is hung back on the trail side.

follow_through.observation: Finish is slightly unbalanced due to the weight staying back. Lead arm exhibits a slight chicken-wing pattern.

metrics.weight_transfer: Poor — majority of weight remains on trail side at impact
metrics.impact_position: Hands behind the ball with flipped wrists

analysis.key_fault: Early extension and a slightly steep downswing path leading to inconsistent contact and a potential slice/fade ball flight.

drill_1.name: Chair/Wall Drill
drill_1.description: Practice keeping the trail glute against a wall or chair during the backswing and lead glute during the downswing to prevent early extension. Do 20 slow practice reps.

drill_2.name: Pump Drill
drill_2.description: From the top of the backswing, pump the hands down to hip level twice while keeping the hips back, then swing through on the third downswing. Do 15 reps.

drill_3.name: Alignment Stick in Ground
drill_3.description: Place an alignment stick angled behind you to encourage an under-the-stick (inside-out) path. Spend 10 minutes making slow-motion swings.

analysis.summary: Your swing shows a solid athletic foundation at setup. The primary areas for improvement are maintaining your spine angle through impact (avoiding early extension) and smoothing out the transition to prevent a steep downswing path.

setup.observation: Stance width is appropriate for a driver. Good spine angle and knee flex. Ball position is correctly forward in the stance.

backswing.observation: Takeaway is slightly inside, leading to a somewhat steep position at the top. Shoulder turn is decent but could be deeper.

downswing.observation: Transition is initiated slightly by the upper body, causing a steep, out-to-in path. Hips move toward the ball early.

impact.observation: Early extension is present as the hips humped toward the ball, causing the spine to straighten and hands to raise at impact.

follow_through.observation: Finish is relatively balanced with good weight transfer to the lead side, though slightly upright due to early extension.

metrics.weight_transfer: good â 75% lead side at finish
metrics.impact_position: hips slightly cleared, spine angle extended

analysis.key_fault: Over-the-top transition leading to a steep, out-to-in swing path and early extension.

drill_1.name: Pump Drill
drill_1.description: Take the club to the top of the backswing, then bring it down halfway to feel the arms dropping straight down before rotating. Do this 3 times before making a full swing.

drill_2.name: Alignment Stick in the Ground
drill_2.description: Place an alignment stick in the ground behind you at the same angle as your club shaft. Practice swinging under the stick on the downswing to prevent the over-the-top move.

drill_3.name: Butt-to-Wall Drill
drill_3.description: Stand a few inches away from a wall in your posture. During the backswing and downswing, keep your glutes in contact with the wall to prevent early extension.

analysis.summary: Your swing shows athletic potential with a solid setup and good rotation. However, the transition is initiated primarily by the upper body, causing an over-the-top path and early extension at impact. Focusing on dropping the hands and maintaining spine angle will greatly improve consistency.

setup.observation: Stance is wide and athletic, suitable for a driver. Spine angle is decent, though slightly rounded in the upper back. Ball position is forward.

backswing.observation: Club is taken back slightly inside, leading to a lift at the top. Shoulder turn is decent but could be deeper.

downswing.observation: The transition starts with the upper body and shoulders, casting the club outward and creating a steep, over-the-top path.

impact.observation: Early extension is present as the hips move toward the ball, causing the spine to straighten and leading to a slightly unstable impact position.

follow_through.observation: Good rotation through the ball, finishing with weight mostly on the lead side, though balance is slightly lost at the very end.

improvements: Extremely short and flat backswing limits power potential

analysis.key_fault: Extremely abbreviated backswing and lack of body rotation, resulting in an arm-dominated swing and poor balance.

drill_1.name: L-to-L Drill
drill_1.description: Focus on hinging your wrists to create an 'L' shape between your lead arm and the club shaft halfway back, and mirror this 'L' shape on the follow-through. This helps lengthen the swing and improve wrist hinge.

drill_2.name: Shoulder Turn Drill
drill_2.description: Place a club across your shoulders and practice turning until the lead end of the club points behind the ball. This trains a full shoulder turn and prevents a short, arm-only backswing.

drill_3.name: Hold Your Finish Drill
drill_3.description: Make swings focusing on holding your finish completely balanced on your lead side for 3 seconds. This will prevent you from falling backward or stepping out of the swing.

analysis.summary: Your swing is currently very short and dominated by the arms, which limits your power and causes you to lose balance on the follow-through. By focusing on a fuller shoulder turn and proper wrist hinge (L-to-L drill), you will create a wider, more powerful arc and improve your overall consistency.
